Hi Olga (and Acme team),

Thanks for the details — we can support this placement. A few items we need to confirm with carriers before we can issue a formal binder/endorsement:

1) Exact Additional Insured wording: ISO CG 20 10 is fine, but some carriers will prefer "as required by written contract" language. If Acme has a preferred endorsement text, please share.
2) Retroactive date on the policy/endorsement: most carriers for our market are open to no-retro endorsements for services starting after the inception date; for prior acts E&O carriers may request a retro date. We will check with the primary carriers and advise.
3) Certificate holder / description on the COI: confirm you want the Order Form # and Acme's legal name exactly as it appears on the contract.

Attached is a preliminary quote and carrier list — final terms will depend on underwriting responses. Expect an update by EOD Wednesday.

Folks — quick legal take from my side after reviewing the MSA insurance block and the broker quote:

- Additional Insured: we prefer an endorsement that names "Acme Corp, its subsidiaries and affiliates" and is ISO-equivalent. If carrier provides "as required by contract" language only, ask for the exact text and endorsement pages; we need to ensure defense coverage is included.
- Waiver of subrogation: acceptable as requested, subject to carrier consent. Please flag if any carrier has strict anti-waiver rules.
- Retro date: for E&O we are ok with the carrier's requested retro date so long as it does not exclude acts during the initial onboarding period (first 30 days). If underwriter insists on an earlier retro date that effectively cuts off coverage for services we will deliver, we need to escalate.

Operational ask to InsureCo: please get a copy of the actual endorsement wording (PDF) we can attach to the Order Form. A COI alone is not sufficient for legal acceptance unless backed by the endorsement pages.

I redlined one small MSA clause (see attached) to allow the security team 30 days to request supplementary evidence for cyber prior to cutover. Otherwise, the coverage minimums look aligned.

-Aditya
